intuition.title: Staged carbon-dot preparation
intuition.text: A homogeneous 2 g citric-acid-monohydrate/0.6 g reduced-GSH mixture is heated RT→140 °C→180 °C, held 1 h at 180 °C, then cooled, acetone-centrifuged, dialyzed 24 h, 0.22 µm-filtered, freeze-dried and redispersed as a 1 mg/mL aqueous stock. The 140 °C dwell, ramps, acetone amount and yield are unreported.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.2 / printed p.26766, CQD synthesis and Scheme 1 upper row

intuition.title: Structure and method scope
intuition.text: Figure 3A pristine CQDs have 2.1–2.4 nm TEM diameter (mean 2.31 nm), while Figure 4B reports 2.3 nm by DLS for pure CQDs. These methods and specimens are source-linked at the article level, without an asserted shared aliquot.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p.4 / printed p.26768, Figure 3A-B, Figure 4A-B and adjacent characterization prose

intuition.title: No inferred phase
intuition.text: The 0.20 nm Figure 3A HRTEM fringe is assigned by the authors to graphite carbon (100). It does not provide measured coordinates or a unique bulk CQD phase. Figure 3B and larger Figure 4B CQDs/Pro aggregates belong to the downstream assay.

general_background.title: Heating and precursor conversion
general_background.summary: As a mixture is heated, precursor conversion and particle growth can change at different rates. Different activation barriers can make these rates change differently as temperature rises, allowing nucleation and growth to overlap.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
